slides.title:
Korean spirits as
the base, not the twist.
slides.body:
Plenty of bars use a Korean ingredient as a garnish. Here the local bottle is the foundation. The World's 50 Best describes a negroni rebuilt on deodeok — a native mountain root — with Korean bitters, and a drink called Wonju that starts from mowallin, a rice distillate made locally, then adds mezcal, corn cream, corn silk, pepper and egg yolk.

Soju arrives as a shot in traditional clay cups, with a "geonbae" from the team. The room follows the name: cham is the Korean word for oak, and the fittings are oak throughout.

caption:
Cham is the Korean word for oak — and the room is fitted out in it.

Bar Cham, a restored hanok in Seochon, builds its cocktails on Korean spirits: a negroni rebuilt on deodeok root, a drink starting from a rice distillate made in Wonju. No. 33 on Asia's 50 Best Bars 2026, one of four Seoul bars listed.

Hours differ between listings — worth confirming first.

Sources in the last slide. Save it for your next trip.
